data.cultural_impact: In Hindu mythology, Lord Rudra, also known as Shiva, is the god of destruction, transformation, creativity, and regeneration. The name Rudal, with its association with Rudra, represents the warrior spirit and the ability to confront and overcome difficulties. This name is widely used in Hindu communities and is often given to boys as a symbol of strength and courage.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Rudal represents the inner warrior that resides within each of us. It reminds us of our divine potential and the power to transform ourselves and our lives through courage and determination. This name is a reminder to be fearless in the face of challenges and to trust in the divine power within us to overcome any obstacle.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Rudal: Roaring like Rudra, the destructive aspect of Shiva, embracing change and transformation. Dissolving old patterns, ushering new growth.

historical_references.reference: Rudra is a name of Shiva, the god of destruction. He is considered the primordial god, the source of all creation and existence, and the destroyer of all things. In the Rigveda, Rudra is the god of storms, and is often depicted as a wild, fierce deity. The Rigveda refers to Rudra with various epithets, including 'Pashupati' (lord of all creatures), 'Shankara' (benign), and 'Mahadeva' (great god).
historical_references.context: Ancient Hindu texts, specifically the Rigveda

historical_references.reference: The name 'Rudra' is also mentioned in the Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic, as the name of a demon who was a great devotee of Shiva. He is described as a fierce and fearless warrior, and is said to have been blessed by Shiva with the power to assume any form and to grant boons to his devotees. Rudra the demon is also known as Rudra-Kumar, and is said to have aided the Pandava brothers in their fight against the Kauravas.
